dedupe_keys.name: smici database of significant multi domain incidents against critical infrastructure

description: The Significant Multi-domain Incidents against Critical Infrastructure (SMICI) database records cyber-physical and cyber-operational attacks on critical infrastructure, meaning attacks that damage physical assets or physically disrupt operational processes, to help researchers understand attackers' behaviour and the impact of such incidents. It covers incidents worldwide across all critical infrastructure sectors, compiled only from publicly available information, as an event-based, open-source and publicly available database. It was developed by the Unconventional Weapons and Technology Division of START at the University of Maryland. The portal offers a free search tool showing a limited subset of variables with a codebook describing them, and the full raw database is available on request through the contact form; no licence is stated and the site is copyright the University of Maryland. Caveats: public-source coverage misses unreported incidents, and the online tool simplifies the data for general readers. It supports threat scenario design, cascading failure and resilience analysis of cyber-physical risks to energy, water, transport and other infrastructure; a related record is the US National Infrastructure Protection Plan.
